steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Metallic bonding: The strong electrostatic attraction between positive metal ions and the sea of delocalised electrons. Metals form a giant lattice of positive ions surrounded by delocalised electrons. | Delocalised electrons: Electrons that have left their atoms and are free to move throughout the metallic structure. They come from the outer shell of metal atoms. | Alloy: A mixture of a metal with one or more other elements (usually another metal or carbon). Alloys are harder than pure metals because the different-sized atoms disrupt the regular arrangement of ions. | Shape memory alloy: An alloy that can return to its original shape after being deformed when it is heated. Example: Nitinol (nickel-titanium alloy) used in dental braces and stents.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Foundation Describe the structure of a metal and explain what holds the structure together. | Foundation Explain why metals are good conductors of electricity and heat. | Foundation Explain why pure metals are malleable but ionic compounds are brittle.
